cluster_summary: This cluster comprises vulnerabilities where file parsers fail to validate user-controlled integer values (offsets, sizes, counts) before using them in memory writes, loop bounds, or decompression. The lack of bounds checking allows attackers to trigger out-of-bounds writes, infinite loops, memory exhaustion, or CPU exhaustion via crafted files.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata into memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work. Report code paths where protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 11 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work.

mechanism.missing_guard: protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion
mechanism.name: unbounded binary length or size field drives resource use
mechanism.sink_shape: memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add validation checks for non-negative offsets and ensure coordinates are within image dimensions, raising an error if invalid.
sub_patterns.name: Missing validation of tile/image coordinates leading to out-of-bounds write
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code assumes tile offsets or extent coordinates are non-negative and within image bounds, but no validation is performed before using them to compute memory boundaries.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add a maximum output size limit and raise an exception if the decompressed data exceeds the limit.
sub_patterns.name: Unbounded decompression output causing memory exhaustion
sub_patterns.root_cause: Decompression routines (FlateDecode, RunLengthDecode, gzip) do not impose a limit on the size of decompressed output, allowing a decompression bomb to exhaust memory.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Clamp or reject excessive loop bounds; replace iteration over a range with iteration over actual collected object IDs.
sub_patterns.name: Unvalidated loop bounds from input metadata causing CPU exhaustion
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled integer values from PDF stream or trailer dictionaries (e.g., /N, /Size) are used directly as loop bounds without validation or capping, allowing arbitrarily large iterations.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Wrap decompression calls in try/except blocks with fallback, and add a state flag to prevent reuse after an error.
sub_patterns.name: Missing error handling in decompression leading to crash or buffer overflow
sub_patterns.root_cause: Decompression routines do not handle malformed data gracefully: exceptions are uncaught, or the decompressor state is reused after an error, leading to crashes or stack buffer overflows.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add a guard after the seek operation: break out of the loop if the read position does not advance.
sub_patterns.name: Missing validation of computed offset leading to infinite loop
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code subtracts a constant from a user-controlled size field without verifying the result is non-negative, causing a seek operation to move backwards and re-read the same data indefinitely.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add validation of columns and row_length against configured maximums, raising an exception if exceeded.
sub_patterns.name: Missing limits on stream parameters leading to memory exhaustion
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled PDF stream parameters (columns, colors, bits_per_component) are used to compute row_length without validation, enabling arbitrarily large memory allocation.
